q: Which of those can we actually fix?
answer:
Most of the fall is fixable: the largest drivers you can act on are lower ad delivery (ad spend fell) and the orders drop; discounts rose but are also controllable. Together they explain the September vs August gap — AOV did not cause the decline.

Quick reality check (2026-08-02..2026-08-31 → 2026-09-01..2026-09-30)
- Ad spend fell from ₹73,463/day to ₹39,777/day (−45.9%). Actionability: high — you can restore or reallocate budget, re-enable paused campaigns, or shift bids/campaigns; this is the fastest lever to stop order loss.  
- Orders fell from 56.0/day to 31.0/day (−44.6%). Actionability: high — this is the outcome to fix (via ads, landing pages, offers, or conversion fixes). The orders drop is the dominant arithmetic driver of the net‑sales fall.  
- Discounts rose from ₹2,407/day to ₹3,497/day (+45.3%). Actionability: medium — you can tighten promo rules, reduce blanket discounts or fix coupon misuse, but reducing discounts may lower conversion unless replaced with better targeting.  
- Net AOV moved slightly (INR +1.9% per day) and did not cause the decline. Actionability: low priority — optimizing AOV helps margin but won’t restore the lost topline quickly.  
- Cost lines (shipping, gateway, product cost) also moved and are partially actionable (supply, logistics), but they explain margin/cogs more than the topline drop.

Worth checking: which ad platforms and campaigns lost delivery (Meta and Google both dropped; platform-level spend and orders shifted sharply). Next: Break this down by ad platform and campaign

Period: 2026-08-02..2026-08-31 vs 2026-09-01..2026-09-30 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-29
